title: Exactness and shift compatibility of the tensor base-change transformation
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $X,X',S',T,Y$ be schemes. Let $p:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to S'$, $g:T\to S'$, $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to T$ be morphisms with $f'h=ge$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$. Use the unbounded constant-coefficient module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], their derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], and exact inverse images and K-injective direct images with adjunctions as in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Define bifunctors to $D(X'_{\Et},\Lambda)$ by
$$A(E,F)=p^{-1}E\otimes^L_\Lambda(f')^{-1}Rg_*F,\qquad B(E,F)=Rh_*(h^{-1}p^{-1}E\otimes^L_\Lambda e^{-1}F),$$
for $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $F\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Let $\alpha_{E,F}:A(E,F)\to B(E,F)$ be the $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ adjoint of
$$h^{-1}A(E,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}h^{-1}p^{-1}E\otimes^L_\Lambda e^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*F\xrightarrow{1\otimes e^{-1}\varepsilon_{g,F}}h^{-1}p^{-1}E\otimes^L_\Lambda e^{-1}F,$$
where the first map is the inverse of the inverse-image tensor comparison of [def-kun-derived-tensor], invertible by [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], composed with the inverse-image composition isomorphism for $f'h=ge$ of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], and $\varepsilon_g$ is the derived counit. Then $A$ and $B$ are exact functors in each variable [def-weil-triangulated-category], and $\alpha$ is natural in both variables and commutes with their canonical integer-shift comparisons. Precisely, with either variable fixed, writing $C$ for the other input and $\chi_{A,m,C}:A(C[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}A(C)[m]$, and likewise $\chi_B$, one has
$$\chi_{B,m,C}\alpha_{C[m]}=\alpha_C[m]\chi_{A,m,C}\qquad(m\in\mathbf Z).$$
The comparisons are those induced by termwise exact inverse image, K-injective direct image, and the signed total-complex tensor shifts. No assertion that $\alpha$ is invertible is included.

proof.text: All functors here act on the unbounded module derived categories, not just on bounded-below abelian sheaves. By prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, each inverse image is an exact additive module functor and identifies with ringed-topos module pullback, since the pulled-back constant coefficient ring is the constant coefficient ring. Apply lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization to obtain its exact termwise derived functor with the identity comparisons on shifted complexes. The construction in def-kun-unbounded-exchange supplies the unbounded K-injective right derived direct images. Apply lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated to the additive module direct images to obtain exactness with their K-injective shifts. Tensoring with either fixed derived object is exact by lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated. For fixed F, A is tensor with the fixed object (f')^{-1}Rg_*F after p^{-1}; for fixed E it is tensor with p^{-1}E after (f')^{-1}Rg_*. For fixed F, B is Rh_* after tensor with e^{-1}F after h^{-1}p^{-1}; for fixed E it is Rh_* after tensor with h^{-1}p^{-1}E after e^{-1}. Apply lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite to these four composites. This proves separate exactness and identifies the composite comparisons with the chi_A and chi_B specified in the statement.

proof.text: Write L=h^{-1}, R=Rh_*, P=p^{-1}E and V=(f')^{-1}Rg_*F. The first comparison L(P tensor^L V) -> LP tensor^L LV is the canonical inverse tensorator. Use lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit for the ringed-topos morphism induced by h and the constant coefficient rings. It applies without boundedness or properness. Its normalization on flat-term K-flat representatives is exactly the comparison used here: both are the localization of the inverse of the ordinary pullback tensor map on each total-tensor summand. The identification of exact module pullback with inverse image is supplied by prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact; lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization computes this exact pullback termwise with its prescribed shifts. Thus the comparison is not being replaced by a different monoidal structure. By lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal it is invertible, and by the two displayed shift equations of lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit it commutes with shifts in P and in V. After substitution P=p^{-1}E and V=(f')^{-1}Rg_*F, naturality in the shifted input and the composite comparisons give these same equations for shifts of E or F.

proof.text: Let theta:h^{-1}(f')^{-1} -> e^{-1}g^{-1} be the inverse-image composition isomorphism of def-kun-unbounded-exchange. Its definition is termwise descent of the sheaf composition isomorphism. On a representative complex K shifted by m, its degree r component is theta_{K^{r+m}}. The two termwise shifts in its shift square are identities on that object, so the square commutes in every degree, for each integer m, including negative m. Naturality of the sheaf composition isomorphism makes this an equality of chain maps. By lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization these are the canonical derived shift comparisons, and clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property descends the equality to all derived objects. Naturality descends in the same way by clause (2). This argument uses only the given commutative square and its prescribed composition map; it does not apply a bounded-below comparison theorem to an unbounded object.

proof.text:
Put D(E,F)=h^{-1}p^{-1}E tensor^L e^{-1}F, so B=RD, and denote the displayed map LA -> D by beta. Apply lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift to each exact additive module adjunction u^{-1} -| u_* for u=g,h, supplied by prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact and def-kun-unbounded-exchange. Its K-injective existence hypotheses are part of that unbounded construction. Hence both the unit and counit commute with the fixed termwise/K-injective shifts for every integer m. In particular e^{-1}epsilon_g commutes with shifts in F. The tensor shift structure of lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent is natural in arbitrary derived morphisms of the other factor, not only chain maps: therefore 1 tensor e^{-1}epsilon_g commutes with shifts in E as well. Its compatibility in F is its counit shift equation tensored with the fixed first factor. Combine these equations with Steps 2 and 3, cancelling the intermediate shift comparisons. For either varying input C, with a_C:A(C[m])->A(C)[m], d_C:D(C[m])->D(C)[m], and l_M:L(M[m])->LM[m], the result is
$$d_C\,\beta_{C[m]}=\beta_C[m]\,l_{A(C)}\,L(a_C).$$
Each constituent is natural in both inputs: the tensorator, theta and counit are natural, and tensor is a bifunctor. Composition gives naturality of beta.

proof.text:
Let eta be the unit of L -| R. The adjunct formula is alpha_C=R(beta_C) eta_{A(C)}. Thus naturality of beta and eta proves naturality of alpha in each variable, hence bifunctorial naturality. Write r_N:R(N[m])->RN[m] for the canonical K-injective shift. The specified comparison of B=RD is chi_B=r_{D(C)} R(d_C). For either varying input use Step 4 and then naturality of eta, naturality of r, and the unit shift equation from lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift:
$$\begin{aligned}
\chi_B\alpha_{C[m]}
&=r_D R(d_C\beta_{C[m]})\eta_{A(C[m])}\\
&=r_D R(\beta_C[m])R(l_A)RL(a_C)\eta_{A(C[m])}\\
&=r_D R(\beta_C[m])R(l_A)\eta_{A(C)[m]}a_C\\
&=(R\beta_C)[m]r_{LA}R(l_A)\eta_{A(C)[m]}a_C\\
&=(R\beta_C)[m]\eta_{A(C)}[m]a_C
=\alpha_C[m]\chi_A.
\end{aligned}$$
Here A=A(C), D=D(C); composition is read right to left. The unit equation is precisely r_{LA}R(l_A)eta_{A[m]}=eta_A[m]. It holds for the fixed shifts, so the computation gives the requested equality for every m in Z without choosing new comparisons. The same calculation applies with E or F varying. This concludes the argument for the actual specified mate.
